Chant and hymns

Chant and hymns

4 sectionsNot completed
Notes

The texts sung in worship also express Christian teaching. The two resurrection hymns here proclaim Christ’s rising and saving work, while their tone labels connect the words with the Church’s musical traditions.[1]

What does the Tone I resurrection hymn proclaim?[1]

The hymn contrasts the sealed tomb and soldiers’ guard with Christ’s resurrection on the third day. Its praise identifies him as the giver of life and connects resurrection with his kingdom and care for humanity.[1]

Read original passage

Tone I: resurrection hymn

While the stone was sealed by the Jews, and soldiers stood on guard over thy body undefiled, thou didst rise on the third day, O Saviour, who givest life unto the world. For which cause the Heavenly Powers cried aloud unto thee, O Giver of Life: Glory to thy resurrection, O Christ! Glory to thy kingdom! Glory to thy providence, O thou who alone lovest mankind!

What does the Tone VIII hymn proclaim?[1]

This hymn connects Christ’s descent, burial and resurrection with deliverance from the passions. Passions here means disordered impulses from which the hymn speaks of liberation. The words express doctrine in a compact sung form.[1]

Read original passage

Tone VIII: resurrection hymn

Thou didst descend from on high, O Tender-hearted One; thou didst endure the three-days' burial, that thou mightest free us from our passions, O our Life and Resurrection. Glory, O Lord, to thee.

What does the tones tutorial contain?[2]

The OCA tutorial introduces eight tones through musical phrases and examples in Common Obikhod and Kievan chant. It includes written explanations and recorded demonstrations, identifying particular musical traditions rather than presenting every Orthodox chant practice as identical.[2]

Source publication

Tutorial for Learning the Tones

Open source text

A published music collection[3]

The linked OCA music library contains liturgical music resources. It provides a further route from the hymn texts to their published musical settings.[3]
